subject: Business Models
title: Zombie Subscriptions
description: Learn Zombie Subscriptions in one minute.

hook.text: That app you signed up for last year? It's still charging your card. You haven't opened it in 11 months.

buildup.text: Zombie subscriptions are active payments for services the user has completely stopped using.

discovery.text: Americans waste $32 billion annually on forgotten subscriptions. The average person wastes $133/month.

twist.text: Companies know this. Some deliberately make their apps forgettable—quiet charges beat angry cancellations.

climax.text: Banks now offer subscription tracking. Apple shows all active subscriptions in settings to reduce zombie costs.

punchline.text: $133/month wasted on apps you don't use. Check your subscriptions.

quiz.question: How much do Americans waste on forgotten subscriptions annually?

details.summary: Zombie subscriptions are recurring payments that subscribers have forgotten about or no longer actively use but continue paying for due to inertia, hidden billing, or cancellation friction. An estimated 200 million Americans have at least one zombie subscription they are unaware of or ignoring.
details.whyItMatters: Zombie subscriptions represent billions in annual consumer spending on unused services. While they boost short-term retention metrics for companies, they create trust deficits and regulatory risk..
takeaways: Millions of consumers pay for subscriptions they have forgotten about
Autopay and buried billing statements enable zombie subscription persistence
Apps like Trim and Rocket Money help consumers identify and cancel zombies

faq.question: How widespread is the zombie subscription problem?
faq.answer: Studies estimate that 42% of consumers pay for subscriptions they have forgotten about. The average person wastes $133 monthly on unused subscriptions. Credit card autopay hides charges in monthly statements. Low individual amounts reduce the urgency to review and cancel.

faq.question: How are fintech companies building businesses around zombie subscriptions?
faq.answer: Apps like Rocket Money and Trim scan bank statements to identify recurring charges and help users cancel subscriptions. They charge a percentage of money saved or a subscription fee of their own. The irony of subscribing to cancel subscriptions highlights the depth of subscription saturation.
